`sportsdataverse-py` is the Python sister to the SportsDataverse R packages
(`hoopR`, `wehoop`, `cfbfastR`, `baseballr`, `fastRhockey`) and gives you tidy
[polars](https://pola.rs) / [pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org) access to
play-by-play, box score, schedule, roster, and odds data across the NBA, WNBA,
NFL, MLB, NHL, men's & women's college basketball, college football, soccer,
cricket, junior hockey, and more.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
This site is a **Quarto + Great-Docs conversion** of the production
[Docusaurus docs](https://py.sportsdataverse.org), built to evaluate Quarto's
literate, *run-it-for-real* documentation model against the current React/MDX
stack. Every table and number below is the **genuine output of `sportsdataverse`
code executed at build time** and frozen into the static page — no client-side
Python, no hand-maintained "expected output" that can drift. See the
[evaluation write-up](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-py/blob/proto/quarto-docs/docs-quarto/README.md).
:::

## Install

::: {.panel-tabset}

### pip

```bash
pip install sportsdataverse
```

### uv

```bash
uv add sportsdataverse
```

### conda

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge sportsdataverse
```

:::

Requires Python 3.9–3.14. The DataFrame engine is polars 1.x; every loader can
hand back pandas with `return_as_pandas=True`.

## The surface, in one cell

First, import the package and confirm the per-sport namespaces resolve. This is
a stable, offline-safe call — it touches no network.

```{python}
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")  # silence the harmless numexpr/bottleneck UserWarning

import sportsdataverse as sdv

sports = ["nba", "wnba", "nfl", "mlb", "nhl", "mbb", "wbb", "cfb", "odds"]
present = [s for s in sports if hasattr(sdv, s)]
present
```

Each sport submodule exposes an `espn_<sport>_*` family of tidy-data loaders.
For example, the NBA namespace ships a large ESPN endpoint surface:

```{python}
import sportsdataverse.nba as nba

nba_espn = [fn for fn in dir(nba) if fn.startswith("espn_nba_")]
print(f"{len(nba_espn)} espn_nba_* callables; first 12:")
nba_espn[:12]
```

## A real loader → a real DataFrame

Call `espn_nba_teams()` — a stable ESPN teams endpoint — and let Quarto render
the returned **polars** DataFrame as an HTML table. This is *live data captured
at build time*, not a sample that drifts out of date.

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_teams

teams = espn_nba_teams()        # -> polars.DataFrame
teams.select(["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"]).head(10)
```

The cross-league surface is uniform: `espn_<sport>_teams()` returns the same
tidy shape for every league. Here is the NFL equivalent:

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.nfl import espn_nfl_teams

espn_nfl_teams().select(["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"]).head(8)
```

## Inline computed results in prose

Quarto supports **inline executable expressions**, so a sentence can quote a
*computed* number rather than a copy-pasted one that goes stale.

```{python}
n_nba = espn_nba_teams().height
n_nfl = espn_nfl_teams().height
```

As of this render, `sportsdataverse` reports **`{python} n_nba` NBA teams** and
**`{python} n_nfl` NFL teams** from the ESPN teams endpoints — both computed by
Python while this page was being built.
